51165622.title: File:L-14-06-05-A.098- A Clark Construction worker models a properly-fitted safety harness at the National Museum of African American History stand down in Washington, D.C. (14352037252).jpg

ObjectName.value: L-14-06-05-A.098- A Clark Construction worker models a properly-fitted safety harness at the National Museum of African American History stand down in Washington, D.C. (14352037252)

Categories.value: April 2014 in Washington, D.C.|PD US DOL|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|United States photographs taken on 2014-06-05|Standing men in Washington, D.C.|Men with handheld microphones (left) in Washington, D.C.|Files from the U.S. Department of Labor Flickr stream|Clark Construction|National Museum of African American History and Culture - construction|Flickr images missing SDC published in

ImageDescription.value:
5 June 2014 -Washington, DC - The Occupational Safety & Health Administration (OSHA) has participated in an ongoing partnership with construction companies to hold National Safety Stand-Down Fall Protection events. Todays event was held on the site of the new National Museum of African American History & Culture Museum. OSHA Assistant Secretary Dr. David Michaels spoke to the work crew and then watched a "fall" safety harness demonstration by George Stallings (PICTURED LEFT SPEAKING) from Sales Solutions. Brian Flegel, Clark Sr. Vice President and Joe Swank, Clark Construction Executive delivered closing remarks and thanked the construction crew for participating.
